test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 19 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The most essential difference between a DC and AC generator is _______.

options.text: Higher voltages are generated by DC generator only
Higher Voltages are generated by AC generator Only
DC generator has permanent magnet and AC has an electromagnet
DC generator uses a commutator and AC generator uses Slip rings

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **DC generator** uses a **commutator** to convert the generated AC to DC, ensuring a unidirectional output.
 
• An **AC generator** uses **slip rings** instead of a commutator, allowing the output to vary sinusoidally and remain alternating.
 
• The essential difference between AC and DC generators lies in their **mechanisms of current collection**.
 
• In a DC generator, the commutator reverses the connection of the armature coils, converting alternating current into direct current.
 
• In an AC generator, slip rings maintain continuous contact between the rotating armature and the external circuit, allowing for the generation of alternating current.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1:**__ Higher voltages can be generated by both AC and DC generators; the voltage capability depends on design factors rather than being specific to either type.
 
• __**Option 2:**__ AC generators are commonly associated with high-voltage generation, but this is not an exclusive feature, as DC generators can also achieve high voltages.
 
• __**Option 3:**__ Both AC and DC generators can use either permanent magnets or electromagnets depending on the design, making this statement incorrect.
